Al-Naḥḥās compares darkness to a garment and cites al-Nābigha's poem of night pursuing and catching a fugitive. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ traces gh-sh-y through veils, sleep, fainting, dulled sight and insight, rejection in 71:7 and 11:5, the lote tree in 53:16, coverings of senses in 3:154, 8:11, 33:19, 47:20, 2:7 and 45:23, and judgment or punishment in 88:1, 44:10–11, 29:55, 14:50 and 7:41. She notes terror and darkness in 24:40, 10:27, 31:32, 20:78, 13:3, 7:54 and 91:4, and understands this night as deep darkness.
